name: n8n
description: n8n is a powerful workflow-automation tool: connect 400+ apps and APIs, build flows visually, and drop into code whenever you need to. This is a plug-and-play Unraid Community Applications template that wraps the official n8nio/n8n image, tuned with sensible production defaults. Variables with fixed options are dropdowns. IMPORTANT - two one-time setup steps (see the README): 1. DATABASE: this template defaults to PostgreSQL (recommended). Create a database and user first, then fill in the Postgres Host / Database / User / Password fields below. (To use SQLite instead, set DB Type to 'sqlite' and ignore the Postgres fields.) 2. PERMISSIONS: n8n runs as user 'node' (UID 1000) and has no PUID/PGID. Create the AppData folder first, then make it writable by UID 1000 - run once on the Unraid console: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/n8n/files chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/n8n Included defaults: task runners on, execution-history pruning (no DB bloat), binary data stored on disk, telemetry off, and N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false so login works over plain LAN HTTP (set it to true behind HTTPS). Detailed README (full setup & options): https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/Unraid-apps/blob/main/n8n/README.md

paths.name: AppData (n8n data)
paths.description: Persistent n8n data: encryption key, binary data, logs. Create the folder first, then make it writable by UID 1000 - run once: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/n8n/files && chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/n8n

paths.name: Local Files (/files)
paths.description: Optional host folder the Read/Write Files node can access. Create it first (mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/n8n/files) and make it writable by UID 1000 (chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/n8n).

variables.name: DB Type
variables.description: Database type - pick from the dropdown. 'postgresdb' (recommended, template default) or 'sqlite'. For SQLite, select sqlite and leave the Postgres fields empty.

variables.name: Postgres Host
variables.description: Hostname or IP of your PostgreSQL server. The pre-filled 192.168.1.10 is a placeholder - replace it with your Postgres server's IP (or its container name if on a shared Docker network). Required when DB Type is postgresdb.

variables.name: Postgres Database
variables.description: Database name (create it first - see README).

variables.name: Postgres User
variables.description: Database user (create it first - see README).

variables.name: Encryption Key
variables.description: Key used to encrypt stored credentials. Generate a strong one on the Unraid console with: openssl rand -hex 32 - paste the output here and back it up. If left empty, n8n generates one into the AppData folder (persist it, or saved credentials become unreadable).

variables.name: Secure Cookie
variables.description: Pick from the dropdown. 'false' for LAN access over plain HTTP (otherwise the login is blocked); 'true' when running behind HTTPS.

variables.name: Timezone (TZ)
variables.description: Container timezone - pick from the dropdown.

variables.name: Generic Timezone
variables.description: Timezone n8n uses for Schedule/Cron triggers - pick from the dropdown. Keep equal to TZ.

variables.name: Task Runners
variables.description: Run Code-node tasks in a separate runner process (n8n recommended). Pick from the dropdown.

variables.name: Prune Executions
variables.description: Auto-delete old execution history so the database doesn't grow forever. Pick from the dropdown.

variables.name: Execution Max Age (hours)
variables.description: How many hours of execution history to keep when pruning is on (336 = 14 days).

variables.name: Binary Data Mode
variables.description: Where to store binary data - pick from the dropdown: 'filesystem' (recommended, on disk) or 'default' (in the database).

variables.name: Telemetry
variables.description: Anonymous usage diagnostics - pick from the dropdown. 'false' disables telemetry.

variables.name: Webhook URL
variables.description: Public base URL for webhooks behind a reverse proxy. Replace n8n.mydomain.tld with your real domain (note the https:// scheme and trailing slash). Clear this field for LAN-only use.

variables.name: Host
variables.description: Public hostname behind a reverse proxy (no scheme). Replace n8n.mydomain.tld with your real domain. Clear this field for LAN-only use.

variables.name: Protocol
variables.description: Pick from the dropdown. Usually keep 'http' and terminate TLS at your reverse proxy; use 'https' only if n8n itself serves TLS.
